title: Monitoring neural activity during sleep/wake events in adult C.Â elegans by automated sleep detection and stimulation
protocol: Clean microfluidic device and top and bottom glass pieces by rinsing with water.
Rinse microfluidic device, top, and bottom glass pieces with 70% ethanol.
Wipe the rinsed components with a lint-free wipe.
Dry the components in an air stream.
Remove any dust from the components using transparent tape.
Align and secure the cleaned components with binder clips or a microscope slide holder.
Place the assembled microfluidic device in a vacuum desiccator for 30 minutes.
Prepare 200 mL of Saline buffer.
Mix 1 μg/mL fluorescein into 60 mL of the Saline buffer to create Control buffer.
Dissolve 1 mM CuCl2 into another 60 mL of Saline buffer to prepare Copper chloride stimulus solution.
Attach three reservoirs to the reservoir rack stand above the microscope.
Reservoirs are held over the device with a tubing rack stand.
Connect tubing from the reservoirs directly into the device or through the 3-way actuated valve for fluidic control.
Position the device above the objective on the microscope.
Attach tubing to all inlets of the microfluidic device, including the worm loading port and outlet.
Actuate the 3-way valve to direct control fluid to the control1 inlet and the stimulus into the arena.
Adjust reservoir heights as needed to maintain proper flow balance.
Fill each of the 3 reservoirs with their designated solutions (60 mL of Saline buffer, Control buffer, or Copper chloride solution).
Purge all bubbles from the connected tubing using the priming syringe.
Actuate the valve to fill all tubes connected to the 3-way fluidic valve.
Fill the waste reservoir with ≥10 mL Saline buffer.
Use the priming syringe to fill both the outflow waste tube and the outflow outlet tube with buffer.
After 30 min in the vacuum desiccator, remove the device and mount it on the microscope.
Fill microfluidic device with fluid.
Insert the outflow tubing into the waste outlet of the microfluidic device.
Ensure the outflow valve is open and gently push buffer through the device using the priming syringe.
When liquid droplets form at all 4 of the inlets, close the outflow valve.
Insert tubing or a blocking pin into the worm loading inlet.
Gently insert each reservoir’s tubing into the appropriate inlet.
Connect the control reservoir 3-way valve “normally-closed” outlet to the “control1” inlet and its “normally-open” outlet to the “control2” inlet.
Insert tubing approximately 3 mm into the PDMS inlet hole.
Use "drop-to-drop" connections by hanging a droplet from the tubing end to connect with a liquid droplet above the microfluidic port.
Remove excess liquid from the glass using vacuum aspiration or paper towel.
Open the outflow valve to establish flow.
View live images in the microscope and verify that no bubbles are present in the device channels.
Focus on the intersection of inlet channels and observe flow patterns while alternately activating and deactivating the 3-way stimulus valve.
Adjust reservoir heights up or down so that flow from Saline buffer and Copper chloride solution are equal.
Ensure flow from Control buffer enables complete switching between Saline buffer and Copper chloride solution into the downstream imaging area.
Avoid introducing bubbles into the device during preparation.
Ensure that the outflow valve is open only when all ports are connected to tubing or blocking pins.
Close the outflow valve whenever any tubing adjustments are made.
Transfer one young adult C. elegans to an unseeded NGM agar plate.
Flood the NGM plate about halfway with Saline buffer.
Fill the worm loading syringe with ∼1 mL Saline buffer and purge bubbles.
Draw an animal into the worm loading syringe using a drop-to-drop connection.
Submerge the tip of the worm loading syringe under the saline solution.
Gently draw the swimming animal into the tubing section of the syringe.
Close the outlet valve to cease flow through the microfluidic device.
Connect the worm loading tubing to the microfluidic device.
Remove the blocking pin from the worm loading inlet and allow a small droplet to form.
Insert the worm loading tubing with a drop-to-drop connection.
Remove excess liquid from the glass by aspiration or paper towel.
Establish fluid flow in the microfluidic arena.
Open the outlet valve to resume flow.
Insert worm into the microfluidic arena.
Verify that saline buffer is present in the imaging arena.
Apply gentle pressure to the worm loading syringe plunger until the animal enters the arena.
Monitor the animal for 1–2 min to ensure behavior is normal and the animal is healthy.
Set testing parameters and run experiment.
Capture a single image frame of the arena under brightfield illumination with the animal visible.
Import the image frame at 25% scale using the “ImageJ” toolbar in “Micro-Manager.”
Draw a rectangle spanning the outermost points of the arena where the animal will roam.
Record the dimensions (x, y, w, h) of the selection box.
Open the “SleepDetection.ijm” file and edit the variables x, y, w, and h near the top to define the selected area of interest.
Save the edited “SleepDetection.ijm” file.
Locate the “User Defined Closed Loop Settings.txt” file on the computer.
Set parameters as desired in the settings file.
Define imaging resolution with bin 2 setting.
Set framerate to 10 frames per second with 100 ms exposure time.
Configure illumination timing for brightfield at 20 ms and fluorescence at 10 ms with a 5 ms delay from exposure onset.
Capture 300 frames (or 30 seconds) for stimulation recordings.
Program a 10 second chemical pulse starting from frame 50 to 150 or from 5 to 15 seconds within each recording trial.
Monitor sleep state changes using a 10-second interval, with transitions persisting for 3 intervals (30 seconds) to be registered.
Wait 15 minutes after each stimulation trial before triggering the next one.
Begin the next trigger following an opposite transition from Sleep-to-wake or Wake-to-sleep.
Run "ClosedLoopSleepStim.bsh" within Micro-Manager to start the experiment.
Monitor animals for escape attempts through the worm entry port during the first few minutes of the experiment.
Use the worm loading syringe to gently push the animal back into view if it escapes.
Load a new animal if necessary when an escape occurs.
Allow the experiment to run unattended once the animal is well established in the arena.
